# Changelog

What was added or changed in OpenBGA Environmental LIMS, newest first. Changes are
grouped by the calendar month they were merged in and ranked from high to low impact.
The same list is shown in the application under What's new.

## November 2026 (2026-11-11 to 2026-11-26)

### High impact

- **Added:** Download the original file from a confirmed result import (2026-11-24, Batches & QC)

  Open Import source files on an analytical batch to download the exact CSV, TSV or Excel workbook used in a new confirmed import. A workbook download includes every sheet. Earlier imports retain their existing audit and row details.

  Technical notes:

  > Migration `analytical.0015` stores one copy of each confirmed upload in PostgreSQL, up to 1 MiB per import. Include this growth in database and backup sizing. The stored-file verifier checks the files alongside their import events. Keep the migrated schema when rolling back application code after files have been stored.

- **Added:** Record actual instrument injection order (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  Analysts can record the injection order from an instrument run on an analytical batch. Staff can see the nearest verification before and after each sample and open earlier versions when an analyst corrects a transcription.

  Technical notes:

  > Migration analytical.0014 adds an append-only table for sequence versions. Keep the migrated schema if rolling back application code after staff have recorded a sequence.

- **Added:** Calculate daily mass loading from an issued result (2026-11-19, Client portal)

  Clients can open Daily load from a water or wastewater result on their current report. Enter the corresponding sampling-day flow to see the calculation in pounds per day and open the issued PDF to check the source.

- **Added:** Check monthly concentrations at a sampling location (2026-11-19, Reports)

  Clients can open Monthly concentrations beside an issued water or wastewater result to see the sampled days and source reports. With one eligible result per sampled day, the worksheet shows the monthly arithmetic mean and highest daily concentration in mg/L. When a result or sampling interval prevents calculation, the worksheet explains why.

- **Added:** Compare results at a sampling location with a client upper limit (2026-11-19, Client portal)

  From a sampling location’s result history, clients can enter an upper limit in the issued unit and see which comparable results fall above, at or below it. Each row links to its issued PDF and explains when a comparison cannot be made.

- **Added:** Download an issued report package with the QC summary requested at receipt (2026-11-19, Reports)

  Clients can download the stored PDF and results CSV together from the report’s version history. Staff can request a QC summary on a chain of custody and check which samples it covers before release. Each issued version keeps its own selection.

  Technical notes:

  > Receipt migration 0014 adds an order preference that defaults to off for existing and new orders. Packages for versions issued before the migration contain the original PDF and standard results CSV.

- **Added:** Download issued invoice lines for accounting (2026-11-18, Draft invoices)

  Project managers and administrators can download an accounting CSV from an issued invoice. It includes one row per charge with the original billing references, quantities and signed USD amounts. Voiding the invoice closes the download.

- **Added:** Download issued results as a CSV (2026-11-18, Client portal)

  Clients can download the results from an issued report as a CSV. Version history includes a download for each earlier issue, so clients can retrieve the values the laboratory reported before an amendment.

- **Added:** Follow issued results by sampling location (2026-11-18, Reports)

  Open a sampling location on an issued report to see its results over time in the same project. Filter by analyte and open the issued PDF for any row from the latest version of each report. Sortable tables now keep the active sort arrow visible when column controls are available.

- **Added:** Issue a numbered invoice and download its PDF (2026-11-17, Draft invoices)

  Project managers and administrators can issue a reviewed draft and download the original invoice for delivery. To correct an issued invoice, void it with a reason and prepare a new draft from the order. The original PDF and history remain available.

  Technical notes:

  > Migration `commercial.0011` stores issued invoice snapshots and PDF bytes in PostgreSQL. Keep this schema on rollback after the first issuance. See the invoice backup and restore checks in the operations guide.

- **Added:** Record tax amounts on draft invoices (2026-11-17, Draft invoices)

  Project managers and administrators can add a Tax line with an externally determined amount and its basis in the description. The amount is included in the draft total and retained through reasoned edits and cancellation. Review recorded tax when charges change; the application does not calculate or recalculate it.

  Technical notes:

  > Migration commercial.0010 expands the invoice line constraint without changing existing records. Keep the schema on code rollback and use compatible code to display or edit tax lines. Reversal refuses while any tax line exists, including zero amounts and cancelled drafts; do not remove or relabel assessments to force reversal. No dependency or setting changes.

- **Changed:** The application is now called OpenBGA Environmental LIMS (2026-11-17, [#19](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/19))

  The product is now named OpenBGA Environmental LIMS. The new name and logo lock-up appear in the top bar, page titles, footer and in-app help. On narrow screens the top bar shows the mark and keeps the full name for screen readers.

  Technical notes:

  > No behavior, data or migration changes. The default `SOURCE_CODE_URL` and the project name in `pyproject.toml` now use the new repository name, and the default acceptance evidence folder is `environmental-lims-acceptance-<UTC time>`. A deployment that sets `SOURCE_CODE_URL` itself should check that it points to its published source. Existing service, host, database and logger names are unchanged.

- **Added:** Prepare invoice drafts from received tests (2026-11-16, Draft invoices, [#15](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/15))

  Project managers and administrators can select New draft invoice on a received chain of custody and price it from an active price list. Descriptions, quantities and prices can be changed with a reason, and a draft can be cancelled while its history stays. Drafts are internal worksheets; later receipt corrections or price changes do not rewrite them.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0005 in commercial (two new tables). It cannot be reversed once a draft exists. Keep the schema on a code rollback. Every requested test needs a price; prices are whole-cent USD. The draft snapshots the billing and contact details, the PO, the price-list revision and the original sample and test identities.

- **Added:** Record calibration curves and link them to results (2026-11-16, Batches & QC, [#13](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/13))

  Analysts can record an instrument-reported calibration curve for a batch and test and link it, with an optional calibration verification QC observation, when entering or correcting a result. Reviewers can open the standard points and source. If a linked QC observation is later superseded, the result is held from submission, approval and release until a new revision is entered.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0013 in analytical (additive; the reverse is refused once evidence exists). Keep the new schema on a code rollback, and do not review or release linked work with older code. People who contributed the curve or check cannot review or release that result. Grid, file-import and BOD bottle entry do not link evidence. Curve fitting is not included.

- **Added:** Import results from a selected Excel worksheet (2026-11-15, Import mappings, [#12](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/12))

  Analysts can now import an XLSX worksheet using an existing long or wide import mapping. The preview shows the exact values to be stored with their worksheet and row, nothing is written until you confirm, and each worksheet of a workbook is a separate import that cannot be repeated.

  Technical notes:

  > New dependency `defusedxml` (run `uv sync --frozen`); no migration. Identifiers and analysis times must be text. Formulas, merged cells, typed dates, macro-enabled, encrypted or externally linked workbooks and oversized files are refused; hidden rows and columns are included. The 2,000 result limit now also applies after wide rows are expanded in CSV and TSV imports.

- **Added:** Calculated results with kept readings and the laboratory's own rounding (2026-11-14, Batches & QC, [#7](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/7))

  An administrator can set a calculation rule for a test, such as reading times dilution factor or solids by weight. Entering that test then takes the bench readings, works out the result, rounds it once by the laboratory's own rule and keeps a worksheet with the result. Rounding is chosen per test, with no default, and typed or imported results are never rounded.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0010 in analytical (three new tables for calculation rules, worksheets and readings; the worksheet tables cannot be changed or deleted). The reverse is refused while any worksheet exists. File imports and QC sample measurements still supply typed values.

- **Added:** Holding-time limits can be set for a single analyte (2026-11-14, QC configuration, [#6](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/6))

  A holding-time rule under QC configuration can now name a single analyte, for methods whose analytes have different limits (for example EPA 300.0, with 48 hours for nitrate and 28 days for chloride). It replaces the method-wide rule for that analyte; rules without an analyte apply as before.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0009 in analytical (a nullable analyte column and a new uniqueness rule; needs PostgreSQL 15 or later). It cannot be reversed while any rule names an analyte, so create analyte rules only after no older instance runs against the database. Spreadsheet import takes an optional `analyte` column. The starter files now carry per-analyte limits for EPA 300.0 and EPA 365.1. Recorded evaluations are not recalculated.

- **Added:** Acceptance run command that writes evidence after install and upgrade (2026-11-13, [#4](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/4))

  After installing or upgrading, a deployer can run a scripted check of the main controls, such as role refusals, client isolation, independent review and report immutability. It uses synthetic records in a scratch database and writes an evidence package to keep; it is not a statement of validation, compliance or accreditation.

  Technical notes:

  > Run `python manage.py run_acceptance --operator "Your Name" --output /path/to/new-directory`. It runs 23 steps under the deployment's own settings (use `DEBUG=false`), creates and drops a database named `acceptance_<database name>`, and never touches the laboratory's records. The database role needs `CREATEDB`; otherwise supply an empty database in `ACCEPTANCE_DATABASE_URL`. The package holds the report as HTML and PDF, JSON, report PDFs and a SHA-256 manifest. See `docs/operations.md`.

- **Added:** Import setup records from spreadsheets (2026-11-13, Spreadsheet import, [#4](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/4))

  Under Setup, Spreadsheet import, project managers load clients and projects, and administrators also load analytes, methods, tests, QC requirements, holding-time rules, QC limits and preservation rules from CSV files. Each file is previewed row by row and saved all or nothing, and rows use the names and codes people use, never database IDs.

  Technical notes:

  > New app `dataimport`; no migrations. Files are CSV only so that limits stay exact decimals. Each record's history names the file it came from.

- **Changed:** New Evergreen look across the whole workspace (2026-11-13, [#5](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/5))

  Every page has a new design with a light sage shell, status pills with icons, dark mode and a collapsible icon sidebar. The dashboard shows work queues as five lanes, record pages show key facts in a full-width grid under a progress tracker, and lists fit 1280 and 1440 pixel screens without side scrolling.

  Technical notes:

  > No dependency changes. The stack is unchanged (Django, HTMX, Bootstrap 5.3).

- **Added:** Laboratory address, logo and certificate numbers on reports (2026-11-12, Laboratory profile, [#3](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/3))

  Administrators can record the laboratory's address, phone, email, website, logo and certificates under Setup, Laboratory profile. New reports then print a letterhead on the first page and a "Laboratory certificates" section near the end. A certificate prints only when marked for printing and within its validity, and the application does not check results against its scope.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0005 in core (backward compatible; new columns have database defaults). Pillow is now a direct dependency (it was already installed). The logo is stored once per distinct file and cannot be changed or deleted afterwards. A laboratory that records nothing gets the report it had before, and issued reports and their PDFs are untouched.

- **Added:** Post announcements on the sign-in page, dashboard and client portal (2026-11-12, Announcements)

  Administrators can post notices under Setup, Announcements. They appear on the sign-in page, the staff dashboard and the client portal home page, with an optional end time. Withdrawing a notice is permanent, and posting, changing and withdrawing are recorded in the history.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0004 in core (the announcement table).

- **Added:** First public release of OpenBGA Environmental LIMS (2026-11-11)

  A free, open-source LIMS for commercial US water, wastewater and soil laboratories, with one laboratory per deployment. Staff handle sample receipt, batches with QC, independent technical review, explicit release authorization and versioned, immutable PDF reports. Clients sign in to a portal where each sees only its own projects, samples, quotes, submissions and reports.

  Technical notes:

  > Django and PostgreSQL 17 with Bootstrap and HTMX, licensed AGPL-3.0-only. Run `migrate`, then `setup_lab` to create the laboratory, role groups and the first administrator. `seed_demo` loads synthetic demonstration accounts and records; keep it away from a real laboratory database. This software supports laboratory records and does not certify compliance or accreditation.

- **Security:** Stricter browser security headers and request size limit (2026-11-11)

  Browser protections are stricter: every page now sends a Content Security Policy, requests that declare a body over 12 MiB are refused, and searching in the administration screens can no longer be used to probe stored authenticator secrets.

  Technical notes:

  > No migration. New optional settings, documented in `docs/operations.md` and `.env.example`: `CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` (replaces the default policy), `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` (12 MiB by default), `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS`, `SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` and `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (set it only where the platform supplies a client-address header that clients cannot forge). A deployment that adds its own scripts or embeds content may need to adjust the policy.

### Medium impact

- **Changed:** Check historical report logos after a restore (2026-11-26, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can identify an issued report whose original laboratory logo is missing or has different image details after a restore. The check also covers superseded report versions.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Under Report PDFs, the command identifies the version whose saved logo checksum, image type or dimensions do not match a stored logo. The Laboratory logos count still counts each stored image once.

- **Fixed:** Check invoice void history after a restore (2026-11-26, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can find a restored invoice whose status disagrees with its void history, including one still marked issued after a recorded void. The check also verifies who voided the invoice and the reason they gave.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files against the restored database. The Issued invoice PDFs category identifies the invoice, draft or audit event to investigate. Valid inventories keep the same version 1 digest.

- **Fixed:** Check restored files at one point in time (2026-11-26, Installation and upgrades)

  When staff add files during a restore check, the counts and inventory now reflect the files present at the first database read. Run the check again to include later files.

  Technical notes:

  > A standalone verify_stored_files run uses one read-only PostgreSQL transaction across all categories. To capture an inventory at the same point as a backup, pass the same exported snapshot to the command and pg_dump.

- **Changed:** Check worksheet history after restoring a backup (2026-11-26, Installation and upgrades)

  The upgrade report now confirms that a restored result worksheet and one of its original readings each rejected an edit and a deletion. The rehearsal repeats both checks after applying the candidate migrations.

  Technical notes:

  > Read the application job’s upgrade notes for the tested revisions. Both stages run on a disposable copy of the synthetic database.

- **Added:** Compare restored files with the backup inventory (2026-11-26, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can check a restored database directly against the file inventory saved with its backup. The check names each category whose count changed or whose files differ at the same count.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files --compare-manifest source-files.json on the isolated restore before upgrading it. The command exits with an error if file verification fails, the inventory is unreadable or incompatible, or the inventories differ. Use a version 1 inventory with the same file categories as the restored application.

- **Changed:** Trace attachments from each nonconformance step after a restore (2026-11-26, Backup and restore)

  Each new audit entry for opening a nonconformance, changing its status or reopening it identifies the timeline step and any file attached to it. After restoring a backup, deployers can use that entry to identify a missing or replaced attachment.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. For opening and status entries recorded before this change, compare against the file inventory saved with the backup to detect a missing attachment.

- **Changed:** Verify result revision history after a restore (2026-11-26, Installation and upgrades)

  The upgrade report now confirms that PostgreSQL protected the observation text on an open result revision and the review note on an approved revision. It also confirms that both revisions rejected deletion after restore and again after migration.

  Technical notes:

  > The rehearsal checks revisions from the backed-up synthetic installation. Both stages run on the disposable restored database.

- **Fixed:** Verify the original issue time of restored invoices (2026-11-26, Draft invoices)

  The restore check now flags an invoice whose issue time differs from its audit record. For a voided invoice, it also checks that the void history still identifies the original issuer and issue time.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Under Issued invoice PDFs, an invoice fails verification if its recorded issue time differs from the original issue event, or if either side of the void event gives a different issue time or issuer.

- **Changed:** Check restored reports against their release history (2026-11-25, Backup and restore)

  After restoring a backup, deployers can check that each issued report PDF and its frozen results match the original release or amendment event. The check also identifies an event whose issued version is missing.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. A missing, duplicate or inconsistent event fails the check. The command reports the affected version or audit event ID under Report PDFs.

- **Changed:** Check restored subcontract PDFs against their entry history (2026-11-25, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can check that the original and corrected PDFs for a subcontracted test match the sources that staff recorded. The check also identifies a result entry whose source is missing.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Missing, duplicate or inconsistent entry history fails the check. Look under Subcontract source PDFs for the affected result or audit event ID.

- **Changed:** Check restored training attachments against their original records (2026-11-25, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can detect a missing training attachment even when the restored database has also lost the training record. The restore check compares each attached file with the event that recorded it, including corrections.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database and look under Training record evidence. Use the reported training record or audit event ID to investigate.

- **Fixed:** Trace missing invoices and verify who issued them after a restore (2026-11-25, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can find a missing invoice from its issue history even when the restored database has also lost the draft. For issued and voided invoices, the restore check now verifies who issued the original document.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Under Issued invoice PDFs, use the reported invoice, draft or audit event ID to investigate a discrepancy. Intact backups keep the same version 1 file inventory.

- **Changed:** Verify calibration and maintenance attachments after a restore (2026-11-25, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can trace a missing or changed equipment attachment to the audit entry for the original work or correction. The check can identify a missing calibration certificate or maintenance file even when the equipment event was also lost.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Under Equipment event evidence, use the reported equipment event or audit event ID to investigate a discrepancy.

- **Changed:** Verify nonconformance note attachments after a restore (2026-11-25, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can trace a changed or missing file on a nonconformance note to the staff member and audit entry that recorded it. A surviving audit entry can also reveal that the entire note is missing.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Under Nonconformance event evidence, use the reported timeline or audit event ID to investigate a discrepancy.

- **Changed:** Check restored deliverable ZIPs against their export history (2026-11-24, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can check that a restored electronic data deliverable is the ZIP originally generated for an issued report version. The check also flags an export whose ZIP record is missing.

  Technical notes:

  > Run python manage.py verify_stored_files on the restored database. Each ZIP must match one export event by ZIP checksum, report number, version number and report content checksum. A discrepancy fails the EDD export ZIPs check and prevents the command from writing a file inventory.

- **Changed:** Check restored invoice PDFs against their issue history (2026-11-24, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can check whether an invoice PDF in a restored backup matches the one originally issued, even after a void. The check also identifies invoices with missing or duplicate issue events.

  Technical notes:

  > Run `python manage.py verify_stored_files` on the restored database. Each invoice number and PDF checksum must match the original issue event for its draft. A failed check reports the issued invoice record ID and prevents the command from writing a file inventory.

- **Added:** Check stored files at the same snapshot as a backup (2026-11-24, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can take a PostgreSQL backup and a matching inventory of stored files while staff continue working. After restoring the backup, they can compare inventories to detect missing or changed files.

  Technical notes:

  > Pass the same exported PostgreSQL snapshot ID to pg_dump and to verify_stored_files with --snapshot. Keep the exporting transaction open until both commands finish. Generate the comparison inventory on the restored database with --format manifest.

- **Added:** Inspect relative standard error for calibration fits through the origin (2026-11-24, Batches & QC)

  Choose Linear through origin in the calibration fit worksheet to see the relative standard error across all recorded standards and replicates. The worksheet shows the degrees of freedom and explains when a zero slope prevents the calculation.

- **Changed:** Verify issued report content after a restore (2026-11-24, Backup and restore)

  Deployers can detect a change to the frozen report content used for client result downloads, even when the stored PDF is intact. The restore check identifies the affected original or amended report version.

  Technical notes:

  > Run `python manage.py verify_stored_files` on the restored database. Each report version must pass both the PDF and content checks to pass under `Report PDFs`. A failure prevents the command from writing a file inventory.

- **Changed:** Verify laboratory attachments after restore and upgrade (2026-11-24)

  The downloadable upgrade report now covers evidence attached to equipment events, staff training records and nonconformance events. It checks that staff can retrieve the original files and that a signed-in client is denied each download.

  Technical notes:

  > The rehearsal attaches three distinct files on the synthetic baseline. After restoring the backup and again after migrating it, CI checks the records, attachment metadata and bytes returned by the staff download route.

- **Added:** Check stored files after restoring a backup (2026-11-23)

  Deployers can check issued documents, electronic deliverables, laboratory logos and evidence attachments on a restored database. The check lists how many records it examined in each category and identifies records with missing or mismatched files.

  Technical notes:

  > With DATABASE_URL set to the restored database, run `python manage.py verify_stored_files`. It compares each stored file with its recorded SHA-256 and any recorded byte count. Keep the output with the restore record and investigate any nonzero exit. The command only reads laboratory records.

- **Added:** Compare stored files before and after a restore (2026-11-23)

  Deployers can save a file inventory with a database backup and compare it with the restored copy. The comparison identifies the affected category when an entire file record is missing or a file has been replaced.

  Technical notes:

  > Run `python manage.py verify_stored_files --format manifest` on the source and restored databases using the same application version. Pause writes while capturing the backup and its source inventory. Save each successful output separately and compare the two files.

- **Added:** See the recovery assessment for a result’s calibration verification (2026-11-23, Batches & QC)

  Open a result revision to see how its linked calibration verification evaluated when the QC observation was entered. You can see the recorded recovery and limits where available, along with whether someone later corrected that observation.

- **Changed:** Verify a restored backup before upgrading (2026-11-23, Deployment)

  The downloadable upgrade rehearsal report shows which synthetic records survived a PostgreSQL restore and the subsequent upgrade. Both stages also check staff and client PDF downloads.

  Technical notes:

  > CI takes a logical backup of the populated distribution-branch database and restores it into a second, empty database. The previous application checks the restored copy before the candidate applies its migrations and repeats the checks. Each stage must verify the same baseline record counts before CI publishes the report.

- **Changed:** Verify history protections after restore and upgrade (2026-11-23)

  Deployers can check the upgrade rehearsal report to see whether PostgreSQL protected audit events, custody events, issued report versions and stored report PDFs at both stages.

  Technical notes:

  > The rehearsal attempts an update and a deletion on one baseline record in each category on the disposable restored copy. Each attempt must raise the expected database error after restore and again after migration before CI publishes the report.

- **Changed:** Check QC history during upgrade rehearsals (2026-11-22)

  The GitHub Actions upgrade rehearsal now checks that QC samples, observations and corrective actions survive migration. It follows a failed observation through reanalysis and correction and verifies that both records still point to the original observation.

- **Changed:** Check receipt records in the upgrade rehearsal (2026-11-22, Deployment)

  The downloadable upgrade report now counts orders, samples and containers checked against the original installation. The rehearsal also follows a corrected client sample ID from receipt through a custody transfer.

  Technical notes:

  > The populated PostgreSQL rehearsal compares all baseline orders, samples and containers after migration. It checks the original receipt, correction history and transfer for one synthetic sample.

- **Added:** Check relative standard error for a quadratic calibration (2026-11-22, Batches & QC)

  Choose Quadratic on the calibration fit worksheet to see the relative standard error across all recorded standards, including replicates. The worksheet shows the degrees of freedom and explains when a standard or the number of points prevents the calculation.

- **Changed:** Check subcontracted results during upgrade rehearsals (2026-11-22)

  The upgrade rehearsal now follows a subcontracted test through a corrected source report. It checks that staff can retrieve the external laboratory’s original and corrected PDFs and that each issued report version still cites the matching reviewed result.

- **Added:** Choose instrument run-list columns (2026-11-22, Batches & QC)

  Analysts can download an analytical batch’s run list with the column headings and order their instrument needs. Download the example CSV, keep the columns you need and reuse that template for other batches.

- **Added:** Compare inverse-weighted calibration fits through the origin (2026-11-22, Batches & QC)

  In the calibration fit worksheet, staff can choose 1/x or 1/x² weighting for a line with its intercept fixed at zero when their method allows it. The worksheet shows the fitted slope and each standard’s residual and back-calculated concentration. Leaving Weighting blank uses equal weights.

- **Added:** Download tab-separated instrument run lists (2026-11-22, Batches & QC)

  On an analytical batch, open Export run list with a template and choose TSV for an instrument that needs tab-separated columns. The same CSV template sets the headings and column order for either download format.

- **Added:** Download the upgrade rehearsal report (2026-11-22)

  Deployers can download the upgrade notes from a successful GitHub Actions rehearsal. The Markdown report identifies the two tested commits and shows how many synthetic baseline records the upgrade preserved in each category.

  Technical notes:

  > Open the checks run and download the upgrade-rehearsal artifact for the successful application job attempt. Extract upgrade-notes.md to keep a copy with your upgrade records.

- **Added:** Compare calibration standards with a maximum percent error (2026-11-21, Batches & QC)

  In the Calibration fit worksheet, enter a maximum absolute percent error to see which standards exceed it. If your procedure uses a different maximum at the lowest concentration, you can enter that limit for all replicates at that level.

- **Changed:** Read changelog technical notes for a rehearsed upgrade (2026-11-21)

  The GitHub Actions upgrade summary includes new or revised technical notes from the candidate changelog. Open a note’s source at the tested revision to see the change it describes.

- **Added:** See the direction and strength of calibration correlation (2026-11-21, Batches & QC)

  Choose Linear and Unweighted (equal weights) on the calibration fit worksheet to see the Pearson correlation coefficient (r) for the recorded standards. A negative value means response tends to fall as concentration increases. If all responses are equal, the worksheet explains why correlation is unavailable.

- **Added:** Compare back-calculated and recorded calibration concentrations (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  On a recorded calibration, staff can see the concentration each standard’s observed response gives under a linear, through-origin or average-factor fit. The worksheet shows the absolute percent error against the recorded concentration and explains when either value is unavailable.

- **Added:** Compare calibration standards with a line through the origin (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  On a recorded calibration, choose Linear through origin when the method calls for a zero intercept. The worksheet shows the fitted slope, predicted response and signed residual for each standard using equal weights.

- **Added:** Compare external standards by calibration factor (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  On a recorded calibration, staff can see how much instrument response each external standard produces per unit of concentration. The worksheet shows the mean factor, the variation among standards and the residual for each point.

- **Added:** Compare recorded standards with concentrations from a quadratic fit (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  Choose Quadratic in the calibration fit worksheet to compare each standard’s back-calculated concentration with its recorded value and see the absolute percent error. The worksheet explains when the curve turns or is flat, or when a standard’s observed response falls outside the fitted response range.

- **Added:** Compare sample counts between instrument verifications (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  Open a recorded injection sequence to see how many sample injections fall between verifications, before the first or after the last. Enter a maximum to find intervals that exceed it. Missing verifications stay visible in both current and earlier versions.

- **Added:** Inspect relative standard error across calibration standards (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  The calibration fit worksheet shows relative standard error for a free-intercept line or an average calibration factor. Staff can compare the whole fit with their method’s criteria alongside the error for each recorded standard.

- **Added:** Inspect the coefficient of determination for calibration fits (2026-11-20, Batches & QC)

  Choose Linear or Quadratic on the calibration fit worksheet to see how much of the variation in recorded responses the fit explains. The coefficient of determination (R²) uses the selected weighting and includes each replicate. If all responses are equal, the worksheet explains why R² is unavailable.

- **Added:** Compare calibration standards with a linear fit (2026-11-19, Batches & QC)

  Open a recorded calibration and choose equal, inverse concentration or inverse concentration squared weighting. The worksheet shows the slope, intercept and difference between each observed and predicted response in the recorded units.

- **Added:** Compare calibration standards with a quadratic fit (2026-11-19, Batches & QC)

  On a recorded calibration, staff can choose a quadratic fit and inspect its coefficients and the residual for each standard. The worksheet shows whether the fitted response changes direction within the recorded concentration range.

- **Added:** Read upgrade notes for the revisions tested in CI (2026-11-19)

  Open the GitHub Actions checks run for a candidate to see which migrations the upgrade rehearsed and which locked package versions changed. The application job summary links to both tested commits and the candidate’s recovery and acceptance instructions.

- **Added:** Weight same-day grab samples by flow (2026-11-19, Reports)

  On the monthly concentration worksheet, enter the flow at collection for each grab when several eligible samples represent the same day. Use the daily concentrations to check the monthly mean and the highest day against the issued reports.

- **Added:** Choose columns and headings for result CSV downloads (2026-11-18, Reports)

  On an issued report in the client portal, select Use CSV template to download results with the columns your recipient needs. The example template can be edited and reused for current or earlier versions.

- **Added:** Download issued results as an Excel workbook (2026-11-18, Reports)

  Clients can download current and earlier report versions as Excel workbooks. They can reuse their CSV column template to choose which fields appear and how they are labeled and ordered. The workbook keeps sample identifiers and reported values as text, including leading and trailing zeros.

  Technical notes:

  > Excel downloads use XlsxWriter, included in the locked application dependencies.

- **Changed:** Every form opens in the form dialog, including invoice issue and account settings (2026-11-18, Draft invoices)

  Review and issue on a draft invoice, the password change, adding an email address and the two-factor setup, removal and recovery-code forms now open in the same dialog as every other form, over the page you opened them from. Password in the account menu now opens a Password page that shows whether a password is set, with Change password opening the dialog; the two-factor forms have a Cancel that keeps everything as it was.

- **Changed:** Follow up on the oldest returned results first (2026-11-18, Worklist)

  The dashboard shows how long the oldest result has waited since a reviewer returned it. Open Results returned for correction to see the reviewer, time and reason for each return, oldest first. Select the analyte to open the result.

- **Added:** Record and filter explicit due dates on invoice drafts (2026-11-17, Draft invoices, [#23](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/23))

  Project managers and administrators can record an optional due date while editing a draft invoice; setting, changing or clearing it needs a reason, and the earlier value stays in the history. The Draft invoices list shows the date, can be filtered with Due from and Due through, and can be sorted by Due date.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0009 in commercial (a nullable due-date column; existing drafts start undated). It cannot be reversed while any draft has a date. Dates are always entered by hand; payment terms never calculate them. Drafts stay internal, with no issuance, balance, overdue, tax or payment behavior.

- **Added:** See what changed in the application under What's new (2026-11-17)

  Select What's new in the top bar to read the changes to the application, newest first, grouped by month and ranked by impact. A number beside it counts the changes made since you last looked, and opening the list clears it; a new account starts with no number.

  Technical notes:

  > Entries are files in `changelog.d/`; `uv run python manage.py changelog` generates `CHANGELOG.md` and `--check` fails when it is stale. The seen state is a per-user preference, so no migration is needed. Client portal accounts do not have What's new.

- **Added:** Use net payment terms to set an invoice due date (2026-11-17, Draft invoices)

  When issuing an invoice, you can accept a due date calculated from the draft’s Net 15, 30, 45 or 60 terms. An agreed date entered on the draft takes precedence, and you can still issue an invoice without a due date.

- **Added:** Add fees and discounts to invoice drafts with a reason (2026-11-16, Draft invoices, [#18](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/18))

  On an active draft invoice, Add fee or discount lets staff enter a fee or discount with a description, quantity, signed USD price and a reason. These lines are marked as added manually, and an unwanted amount can be corrected to zero with a reason while the line stays in the history.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0008 in commercial (relaxes quote provenance for non-test lines only). It cannot be reversed while manual lines exist, including on cancelled drafts. Older code can read and cancel these drafts but refuses edits.

- **Added:** Carry accepted quote fees and discounts into invoice drafts (2026-11-16, Draft invoices, [#17](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/17))

  An accepted quote that includes fees or discounts can now prepare a draft invoice when its tests and quantities match the received order. Each quoted fee or discount is copied onto the draft once, after the test lines, and staff can edit it with a reason. A draft holds at most 200 lines and cannot have a negative total.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0007 in commercial (a line kind with a default of test; existing lines remain tests). It cannot be reversed while adjustment lines exist. A line's kind and source cannot be edited.

- **Added:** Price invoice drafts from a matching accepted quote (2026-11-16, Draft invoices, [#16](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/16))

  When preparing a draft invoice, staff can choose a matching accepted quote version instead of a price list. The quote must match the received order's tests and quantities with one line per test, and each test takes the quoted price and description. The accepted version stays linked through later edits and cancellation.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0006 in commercial (nullable quote provenance; existing drafts are kept). It cannot be reversed while quote provenance exists, and older code cannot correctly show or edit quote-priced drafts. Matching is done per order; quote quantities are not used up across orders.

- **Added:** Show client account-hold notices at receipt and report release (2026-11-16, Clients, [#14](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/14))

  Project managers and administrators can record an account hold on a client with a required internal note. Staff then see the notice on the client record, the chain of custody, both receipt paths and the report release preview. It is informational: it does not block receipt or release, and hold notes never appear in the client portal or reports.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0013 in receipt (new client fields with defaults; additive). Keep the schema on a code rollback, since older code cannot show the notices.

- **Added:** Calculate BOD5 from retained, analyst-selected bottles (2026-11-15, Batches & QC, [#10](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/10))

  A BOD5 test set up with the bottle calculation opens a worksheet from batch entry or the result record. Analysts keep 1 to 12 bottle observations, enter a seed correction and its source for each, and include or exclude each bottle; the result is the mean of the selected bottles. Excluded observations and the reasons for selection stay with the result.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0012 in analytical (a nullable JSON column for bottle observations); it cannot be reversed once bottle observations exist. The seed correction is supplied, not estimated; bottle suitability, incubation and QC acceptance remain the laboratory's decisions.

- **Added:** Export an analytical batch run list for instrument setup (2026-11-15, Batches & QC, [#11](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/11))

  Analysts and administrators can use Export run list on a batch to download a generic CSV for preparing instrument work, listing every assigned test and directly attached QC sample with catalog limits and sample states. Map the columns to your instrument and check the run: the file does not decide injection order or add standards.

  Technical notes:

  > The file is limited to 2,000 rows and ignores page filters. A closed batch exports its current content, not a historical snapshot.

- **Added:** Keep alkalinity and EDTA hardness titration readings with results (2026-11-15, Batches & QC, [#9](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/9))

  An administrator can select an alkalinity (to pH 4.5, or low alkalinity with two endpoints) or EDTA total hardness calculation for a test. Analysts then enter the burette readings, sample volume and titrant normality, and the result in mg/L as CaCO3 is worked out and kept with its worksheet. A correction keeps the earlier worksheet.

  Technical notes:

  > Alkalinity also keeps the measured endpoint pH. The equations follow EPA 310.1 and EPA 130.2 as historical sources; this does not claim current regulatory approval.

- **Added:** Preparation factors and dry-weight results worked from bench readings (2026-11-15, Batches & QC, [#8](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/8))

  New calculations work out results read from a prepared solution (digest, extract or concentrated portion) from the sample volume or weight and the final volume. Soil results can be corrected to dry weight using the percent solids you enter and its source, and percent solids and moisture are worked out from dish weights. A laboratory chooses the calculation for each test.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0011 in analytical (one nullable column on worksheets for the limit before rounding); it cannot be reversed while any worksheet holds such a limit. Existing calculations and worksheets are unchanged. Dry weight is never inferred.

- **Changed:** Page help now starts with a summary and common tasks (2026-11-13, [#5](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/5))

  The help drawer on every page now opens with a short summary, the common tasks written with the exact button labels and a "Good to know" list, above the full reference of fields and actions. A filter helps you find a topic quickly.

- **Changed:** Redesigned PDF report with an at-a-glance box and clearer amendments (2026-11-13, Reports, [#5](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/5))

  Newly issued PDF reports use a new design: an "At a glance" box at the start, flagged results explained under their rows, amended values struck through beside the new value, and QC issues tied to the results they affect. Reports already issued keep their stored PDF exactly as issued.

- **Changed:** Searchable selects, shared date pickers and remembered list settings (2026-11-13, [#5](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/5))

  Selects offer search on long lists, chips for several choices and a clear button, and long lists of records load as you type. Dates and times use one picker with typed entry, Today and Now shortcuts and the laboratory's time zone, and file uploads use a drop zone. Your list page size, columns, sort order and sidebar state are remembered between visits.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0006 in core (additive; a per-user preferences table).

- **Added:** Sign-in activity is written to the application log (2026-11-13, [#4](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/4))

  A deployer can now see who signed in and when attempts failed: completed sign-ins, failed attempts and sign-outs are written to the application log. Submitted passwords and codes are never logged.

  Technical notes:

  > Lines are written to standard output by the `roots.signin` logger, with the stored username (an unknown or ambiguous identifier shows as unknown). Password attempts refused by the rate limit, rejected email sign-in codes and rejected two-factor codes count as failures. Every application log line also carries `render_request_id`, the validated hosting-platform request header, beside `request_id`; `docs/operations.md` explains how to search them.

- **Added:** Starter files for common water and wastewater methods (2026-11-13, Spreadsheet import, [#4](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/4))

  The Spreadsheet import page offers starter files to check, edit and import: method versions, analytes, tests, holding-time and preservation rules, and fortified blank and matrix recovery limits for EPA 200.7, 200.8, 245.1 and 300.0, each quoting its public source. They are starting points, not laboratory policy; check every row against your own methods, permits and current rules.

  Technical notes:

  > The files carry no reporting limits, soil tests or preparation methods.

- **Changed:** Staff menus now show only the work each role can do (2026-11-12, [#2](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/2))

  The sidebar now shows only the work your roles allow, and sections with nothing to show are left out. For example, an approver sees Dashboard, Reports, Training and Nonconformances, and an analyst sees bench work without receipt, technical review or report management. Someone with several roles sees the combined menu.

  Technical notes:

  > The menu is built from each account's roles and release permission. Access is still enforced on the server, and the client portal is unchanged.

- **Fixed:** Accessibility fixes and clearer history, stock times and external results (2026-11-11)

  Keyboard focus is easier to see and is no longer hidden behind sticky action rows, and the top bar fits at 200% text size. Pages now say when your role cannot use a form instead of offering an action that fails. History shows readable titles, and stock movement times show the time zone.

- **Fixed:** Safer release, disposal and import when several people work at once (2026-11-11)

  Removing someone's release permission can no longer be bypassed by a release already in progress, and the strict CSV import refuses a stale preview or a file already imported into the batch. Three cases that used to end in a server error now show a message instead.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0012 in receipt, which makes sample disposal records final in the database; existing rows are not rewritten.

### Low impact

- **Changed:** Check electronic deliverable downloads after restore and upgrade (2026-11-23)

  The upgrade rehearsal report now covers a synthetic electronic data deliverable. It records whether the owning client could download the original ZIP after a backup was restored and again after the application was upgraded.

  Technical notes:

  > The rehearsal compares the stored export, its frozen recipient mappings and its link to the issued report version with the baseline. The downloadable upgrade notes include the export in the verified record counts.

- **Changed:** See stored file checks in upgrade reports (2026-11-23)

  The downloadable upgrade rehearsal report lists how many documents and attachments the upgraded application checked in each category. A zero shows where the synthetic installation had no files to check.

  Technical notes:

  > To save counts from your own restored database, run `python manage.py verify_stored_files --format json` and redirect standard output to a file. Check the exit status for success. Details of failing records go to standard error.

- **Fixed:** Result entry grid skips untouched rows and gives clearer errors (2026-11-14, Batches & QC, [#7](https://github.com/openbga/environmental-lims/pull/7))

  On the result entry grid, a row left with only the reporting limit the page filled in is now skipped instead of failing, and a blank result reads "Result is required." A stray template comment no longer prints above the grid.

- **Added:** Shared demonstration accounts and a scheduled reset for public demos (2026-11-12)

  A public demonstration can list its demo accounts and shared password on the sign-in page, and its data can be erased and seeded again on a schedule. Demo accounts cannot change their password, email address or two-factor settings. None of this applies to a laboratory's own deployment.

  Technical notes:

  > Adds migration 0004 in accounts (a locked-credentials flag). `seed_demo --announce-accounts` posts the accounts and `DEMO_PASSWORD` (never `demo_admin`; set a different `DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` first). `reset_demo` erases and reseeds in one transaction and runs only with `ALLOW_DEMO_RESET=true`, only on the demonstration laboratory and only when the schema matches the release. A separate demonstration-only deployment blueprint schedules it daily. Never set `ALLOW_DEMO_RESET` where real records are kept.

- **Added:** Demonstration data can include a full synthetic working week (2026-11-11)

  Evaluators can load a full synthetic laboratory: two clients, about 50 samples in every state, a batch awaiting review, a QC failure needing a disposition, control-chart history, an MDL study, and draft, released and amended reports.

  Technical notes:

  > Run `python manage.py seed_demo --full`. It takes about 20 seconds and adds nothing when run again. Plain `seed_demo` is unchanged, and the seed refuses a laboratory that is not the demonstration laboratory.

- **Changed:** Report and portal pages load faster on large reports and many projects (2026-11-11, Reports)

  Report detail and the release preview now open faster on large reports, and the client portal's sample and report lists open faster for clients with many projects.
